import frontend.ast.{Addr(..), Pat(..), Lit(..), BinderId(..)}
import ir.core_ir.{
  CProgram(..), CBind(..), CClause(..), CExpr(..), CStmt(..), CallSite(..),
  CallMode(..)
}
import types.runtime_types.{RuntimeType(..), BinderRow}
import backend.core_validate.{validateBinderStamps, validateCalls}
import support.util.{anyList, joinNl}

sameBinder : BinderId -> BinderId -> Bool
sameBinder (BinderId a n) (BinderId b k) = a == b && n == k

integerLiteral : CExpr -> Option Int
integerLiteral (CLit (LInt n)) = Some n
integerLiteral _ = None

-- Catalog externs use CallDynamic; their known family still emits a direct C call.
arguments : String -> CExpr -> Option (List CExpr)
arguments name (CApp (CVar actual AGlobal) args (CallSite CallDynamic _)) =
  if actual == name then Some args else None
arguments _ _ = None

sourceVar : String -> CExpr -> Bool
sourceVar name (CVar actual (ALocal 0 0)) = actual == name
sourceVar _ _ = False

makeSize : CExpr -> Option Int
makeSize ex = match arguments "byteBlockMake" ex
  Some [n] => match integerLiteral n
    Some count if count >= 0 && count <= 4096 => Some count
    _ => None
  _ => None

leafStatement : String -> Int -> CExpr -> Bool
leafStatement name capacity ex = match arguments "byteBlockSetUnsafe" ex
  Some [i, value, bb] => match (integerLiteral i, integerLiteral value)
    (Some index, Some byte) =>
      sourceVar name bb
        && index >= 0
        && index < capacity
        && byte >= 0
        && byte <= 255
    _ => False
  _ => match arguments "byteBlockBlit" ex
    Some [src, so, dst, do_, n] => match (
      integerLiteral so,
      integerLiteral do_,
      integerLiteral n,
    )
      (Some start, Some dest, Some count) =>
        sourceVar name src
          && sourceVar name dst
          && start >= 0
          && start <= capacity
          && dest >= 0
          && dest <= capacity
          && count >= 0
          && count <= capacity
          && start + count <= capacity
          && dest + count <= capacity
      _ => False
    _ => False

copySize : String -> Int -> CExpr -> Option Int
copySize name capacity ex = match arguments "byteBlockCopyUnsafe" ex
  Some [n, bb] => match integerLiteral n
    Some count if sourceVar name bb && count >= 0 && count <= capacity =>
      Some count
    _ => None
  _ => None

terminal : String -> Int -> CExpr -> Bool
terminal name capacity ex = match arguments "byteBlockGetUnsafe" ex
  Some [i, copy] => match (integerLiteral i, copySize name capacity copy)
    (Some index, Some count) => index >= 0 && index < count
    _ => False
  _ => match arguments "byteBlockLength" ex
    Some [copy] => match copySize name capacity copy
      Some _ => True
      None => False
    _ => False

finish : String -> Int -> List CStmt -> Bool
finish name capacity [CSExpr result] = terminal name capacity result
finish name capacity ((CSExpr ex) :: rest) =
  leafStatement name capacity ex && finish name capacity rest
finish _ _ _ = False

bodyAccepted : CExpr -> Bool
bodyAccepted (CBlock ((CSLet False (PVar name _ _) allocation) :: rest)) =
  name /= "byteBlockMake"
    && name /= "byteBlockCopyUnsafe"
    && name /= "byteBlockGetUnsafe"
    && name /= "byteBlockLength"
    && name /= "byteBlockSetUnsafe"
    && name /= "byteBlockBlit"
    && (match makeSize allocation
      Some count => finish name count rest
      None => False)
bodyAccepted _ = False

sourceFact : CExpr -> List BinderRow -> Bool
sourceFact (CBlock ((CSLet False (PVar name _ bid) _) :: _)) rows =
  anyList
    (row =>
      sameBinder row.brId bid && row.brName == name && row.brType == RTValue)
    rows
sourceFact _ _ = False

export
validateByteBlockKernel : CProgram -> Result String String
validateByteBlockKernel (cp@(CProgram groups ctors ctorTypes impls contexts facts)) =
  let faults = validateBinderStamps cp ++ validateCalls cp
  if faults /= [] then
    Err (joinNl faults)
  else match (groups, ctors, ctorTypes, impls, contexts)
    ([CBind "main" [CClause [] body] _ bid], [], [], [], []) =>
      if anyList
          (row =>
            sameBinder row.brId bid
              && row.brType == RTInt
              && row.brReturns == Some RTInt)
          facts.factBinders
        && sourceFact body facts.factBinders
        && bodyAccepted body then
        Ok
          "(byteblock-kernel v1 runtime-layout=mdk_gc_byteblock_atomic_v1 output=tagged-int source-consumed-by-copy no-escape no-later-argument-allocation)\n"
      else
        Err "byteblock kernel: unsupported producer/use or main return contract"
    _ =>
      Err "byteblock kernel: extra definitions or unsupported module structure"

-- TYPED driver for the Stage 2.4 LLVM de-risking spike (slice 6 — typeclass
-- dispatch).  The typed analog of llvm_emit_main.mdk: it runs the SAME front end
-- `medaka build` ships (desugar → elaborateModules: RKey/EDictAt route stamping
-- + dict_pass leading-dict params → mangleUnitsEv → lower to Core IR), then swaps
-- the final consumer to EMIT textual LLVM IR (llvm_emit.emitProgram) instead of
-- evaluating.  This is the ONLY LLVM driver that produces CMethod/CDict nodes
-- (the plain llvm_emit_main path never marks, so it never dispatches).
--
--   medaka run compiler/entries/llvm_emit_typed_main.mdk <runtime.mdk> <prelude.mdk>... <file.mdk>
--
-- The dispatch fixtures are prelude-free (their own interfaces + impls), so the
-- harness passes ONLY runtime.mdk: elaboration resolves every route without
-- pulling core.mdk's machinery into the emitted module (the spike's scalar subset).
--
-- The mangle step is not optional decoration: typecheck stamps a receiver's
-- record head with the name the MANGLED program will carry, so an emitter side
-- table keyed off the unmangled decls misses every stamped lookup and
-- `core_ir_lower` resolves the record by a bare-label first-match guess (the
-- wrong-slot behaviour issue #38 closed).  Elaborate, mangle, then key every
-- table off the mangled decls — the order `entry_support.emitModulesWith` runs.
import frontend.ast.{Decl(..), Ty(..), Lit(..), BinderId(..), noDeclLoc}
import frontend.parser.{parse}
import frontend.desugar.{desugar}
import types.annotate.{annotateProgram}
import types.typecheck.{
  elaborateModules,
  mainTypeIsUnit,
  mainTypeIsFloat,
  checkedFfiExternTypeNames,
}
import backend.private_mangle.{mangleUnitsEv}
import eval.eval.{funNamesOf, dropShadowedExp}
import ir.core_ir_lower.{
  declaredRecordFieldOrders,
  lowerProgramEmit,
  EmitTarget(..),
  returnsSelfTable,
  selfFnParamTable,
  methodIfaceTable,
  ctorFieldTypeNames,
  externArities,
  validateFfiExternTypeNames,
}
import ir.core_ir.{
  CProgram(..), CBind(..), CClause(..), CExpr(..), DeclFacts(..)
}
import types.runtime_types.{BinderRow(..), RuntimeType(..)}
import backend.llvm_emit.{
  EmitInput, emitProgram, emitProgramRecord, emitProgramWithNativeContract,
  makeEmitInput
}
import backend.native_byteblock_kernel.{validateByteBlockKernel}
import entries.entry_support.{driveRuntime, driveRuntimeArgs, failWith}
import support.util.{contains}
import support.path.{dirOf, joinPath}

export
oracleMain : Unit -> <IO> Unit
oracleMain () = match args ()
  "--byteblock-kernel" :: rest => driveByteBlockKernel rest
  ["--isolation", runtimePath, pPath, pPlusUPath] =>
    emitIsolation runtimePath pPath pPlusUPath
  ["--gap-isolation"] => emitGapIsolation
  _ => driveRuntime emit

-- P -> P+U -> P in one interpreter process. The middle program reuses P's
-- interface/method spellings and adds U, so both semantic inputs and physical
-- caches/counters materially differ between emissions.
emitIsolation : String -> String -> String -> <IO> Unit
emitIsolation runtimePath pPath pPlusUPath =
  let r = do
    runtimeSrc <- readFile runtimePath
    pSrc <- readFile pPath
    pPlusUSrc <- readFile pPlusUPath
    let runtimeDecls = desugar (parse runtimeSrc)
    let pDecls = desugar (parse pSrc)
    let pPlusUDecls = desugar (parse pPlusUSrc)
    let p1 = runEmit runtimeDecls [] pDecls
    let pPlusU = runEmit runtimeDecls [] pPlusUDecls
    let p2 = runEmit runtimeDecls [] pDecls
    if p1 /= p2 then
      Err
        "LLVM emission isolation failure: P changed after same-process P+U emission"
    else if p1 == pPlusU then
      Err "LLVM emission isolation failure: P+U did not produce distinct LLVM"
    else
      Ok (putStr "LLVM_EMIT_ISOLATION_OK\n")
  match r
    Err msg => failWith msg
    Ok v => v

-- Record then strict-emit the same unsupported Core node in ONE process. The
-- record marker reaches stdout before the strict panic; the shell control asserts
-- both, so an ambient Record mode leak changes the second observation to exit 0.
-- `main` is stamped, as every lowered binder is, so the emitter reaches the node.
emitGapIsolation : <IO> Unit
emitGapIsolation =
  let input = makeEmitInput [] [] [] [] [] False False 0 [] [] "" [] []
  let mainId = BinderId "" 0
  let cp =
    CProgram
      [CBind "main" [CClause [] (CMatch (CLit (LInt 0)) [])] noDeclLoc mainId]
      []
      []
      []
      []
      DeclFacts {
        factRequires = [],
        factSupers = [],
        factBinders = [
          BinderRow {
            brId = mainId,
            brName = "main",
            brType = RTValue,
            brReturns = Some RTValue,
            brSigned = False,
          },
        ],
      }
  let (_, gaps) = emitProgramRecord input cp
  if contains "?\tunsupported Core IR node CMatch" gaps then
    let _ = putStr "LLVM_GAP_RECORD_OK\n"
    let _ = emitProgram input cp
    failWith
      "LLVM gap isolation failure: strict emission returned after a recorded gap"
  else
    failWith "LLVM gap isolation failure: record emission did not report CMatch"

emit : List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> <IO> Unit
emit runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls =
  putStr (runEmit runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls)

runEmit : List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> String
runEmit runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls =
  let (input, cp) = prepareEmission runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls
  emitProgram input cp

-- Refuse declarations before lowering can erase them.
driveByteBlockKernel : List String -> <IO> Unit
driveByteBlockKernel [runtimePath, sourcePath] =
  let root = dirOf (dirOf (dirOf (executablePath ())))
  match (
    readFile (joinPath root "stdlib/runtime.mdk"),
    readFile runtimePath,
    readFile sourcePath,
  )
    (Ok canonical, Ok runtime, Ok source) if canonical /= ""
      && canonical == runtime =>
      emitByteBlockKernel
        (desugar (parse canonical))
        []
        (desugar (parse source))
    _ =>
      failWith
        "byteblock kernel: trusted canonical runtime catalog missing or mismatched"
driveByteBlockKernel _ =
  failWith "byteblock kernel: expected runtime catalog and source only"

kernelDeclarations : List Decl -> Bool
kernelDeclarations [DTypeSig False "main" (TyCon "Int" _ _) _, DFunDef False "main" [] _ _ _] =
  True
kernelDeclarations [DFunDef False "main" [] _ _ _, DTypeSig False "main" (TyCon "Int" _ _) _] =
  True
kernelDeclarations _ = False

emitByteBlockKernel : List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> <IO> Unit
emitByteBlockKernel runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls =
  if not (kernelDeclarations userDecls) then
    failWith "byteblock kernel: only main : Int and its body are allowed"
  else match preludeDecls
    [] =>
      let (input, cp) =
        prepareEmissionFor True runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls
      match validateByteBlockKernel cp
        Err message => failWith message
        Ok proof => match (
          getEnv "MEDAKA_BYTEBLOCK_KERNEL_PROOF",
          getEnv "MEDAKA_NATIVE_GC_CONTRACT",
        )
          (Some proofPath, Some reportPath) if proofPath /= ""
            && reportPath /= "" =>
            let (text, report) = emitProgramWithNativeContract input cp
            match (writeFile proofPath proof, writeFile reportPath report)
              (Ok _, Ok _) => putStr text
              _ => failWith "byteblock kernel: cannot write proof/report"
          _ =>
            failWith
              "byteblock kernel: proof and report output paths are required"
    _ => failWith "byteblock kernel: empty prelude required"

prepareEmission : List Decl -> List Decl -> List Decl -> (EmitInput, CProgram)
prepareEmission = prepareEmissionFor False

prepareEmissionFor : Bool ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (EmitInput, CProgram)
prepareEmissionFor addresses runtimeDecls preludeDecls userDecls =
  let livePrelude = dropShadowedExp (funNamesOf userDecls) preludeDecls
  let (coreE, modulesE, _, _, _, _) =
    elaborateModules runtimeDecls livePrelude [("__user__", userDecls)]
  let (coreD, modules2) = mangleUnitsEv coreE modulesE
  let mangled = coreD ++ flatMap snd modules2
  let input =
    makeEmitInput
      (returnsSelfTable mangled)
      (selfFnParamTable mangled)
      (methodIfaceTable mangled)
      (ctorFieldTypeNames mangled)
      (externArities runtimeDecls)
      (mainTypeIsUnit ())
      (mainTypeIsFloat ())
      0
      []
      []
      ""
      (declaredRecordFieldOrders mangled)
      (validateFfiExternTypeNames (checkedFfiExternTypeNames mangled))
  (
    input,
    lowerProgramEmit TargetNative (if addresses then
      annotateProgram mangled
    else
      mangled),
  )

main = oracleMain ()

compiler/backend/native_gc_contract.mdk.text:
-- Native producer observations under Boehm; this report is not a root map.

import frontend.ast.{BinderId(..)}
import types.runtime_types.{BinderRow(..), runtimeTypeName}
import support.util.{joinNl, joinWith, reverseL, escStr, listLen}

public export data StorageKind =
  | TaggedWord
  | RawScalar
  | CodeAddress
  | PackedBytes
  | StackAddress
  | NoValue
  | UnknownStorage
  deriving (Eq, Debug)

public export data LayoutKind =
  | ConstructorCell
  | ClosureCell
  | WordArray
  | DynamicWordArray
  | AtomicBox
  | AtomicByteBlock
  deriving (Eq, Debug)

public export data CallEffect =
  | NoManagedCollection
  | MayCollect
  | MayCollectAndReenter
  | UnknownEffect
  deriving (Eq, Debug)

public export data NativeEvent =
  | Allocation String LayoutKind String String String (List StorageKind) (List String) String
  | Call String String String (List String) (List StorageKind) StorageKind CallEffect
  | Operand String String StorageKind
  | Store String String Int String StorageKind
  | Derived String String String String
  | Uncovered String String
  deriving (Debug)

public export data NativeLog = NativeLog {
  events : Ref (List NativeEvent),
  scope : Ref String,
  nextScope : Ref Int,
}

export
newLog : Unit -> NativeLog
newLog _ =
  NativeLog { events = Ref [], scope = Ref "module", nextScope = Ref 0 }

export
enterScope : NativeLog -> String -> Unit
enterScope log module_ =
  let n = !log.nextScope
  log.nextScope := n + 1
  log.scope := "\{module_}/define\{n}"

export
restoreScope : NativeLog -> String -> Unit
restoreScope log saved = log.scope := saved

export
currentScope : NativeLog -> String
currentScope log = !log.scope

export
recordEvent : NativeLog -> NativeEvent -> Unit
recordEvent log event = log.events := event :: !log.events

export
logEvents : NativeLog -> List NativeEvent
logEvents log = reverseL !log.events

export
taggedSlots : Int -> List StorageKind
taggedSlots n = if n <= 0 then [] else TaggedWord :: taggedSlots (n - 1)

export
constructorSlots : Int -> List StorageKind
constructorSlots n = RawScalar :: taggedSlots n

export
closureSlots : Int -> List StorageKind
closureSlots n = RawScalar :: CodeAddress :: taggedSlots n

-- These are C ABI contracts, not classifications inferred from LLVM i64.
export
helperContract : String -> (List StorageKind, StorageKind, CallEffect)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_make" = ([TaggedWord], TaggedWord, MayCollect)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_copy" =
  ([TaggedWord, TaggedWord], TaggedWord, MayCollect)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_length" =
  ([TaggedWord], TaggedWord, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_get" =
  ([TaggedWord, TaggedWord], TaggedWord, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_set" =
  ([TaggedWord, TaggedWord, TaggedWord], NoValue, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_byteblock_blit" = (
  [TaggedWord, TaggedWord, TaggedWord, TaggedWord, TaggedWord],
  NoValue,
  NoManagedCollection,
)
helperContract "mdk_bit_and" =
  ([RawScalar, RawScalar], RawScalar, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_bit_or" =
  ([RawScalar, RawScalar], RawScalar, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_bit_xor" =
  ([RawScalar, RawScalar], RawScalar, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract "mdk_shift_left" =
  ([RawScalar, RawScalar], RawScalar, MayCollectAndReenter)
helperContract "mdk_shift_right" =
  ([RawScalar, RawScalar], RawScalar, MayCollectAndReenter)
helperContract "mdk_bit_not" = ([RawScalar], RawScalar, NoManagedCollection)
helperContract _ = ([], UnknownStorage, UnknownEffect)

export
runtimeCall : String -> String -> String -> List String -> NativeEvent
runtimeCall scope name result args =
  let (kinds, output, callEffect) = helperContract name
  Call scope name result args kinds output callEffect

allTagged : List StorageKind -> Bool
allTagged [] = True
allTagged (TaggedWord :: rest) = allTagged rest
allTagged _ = False

validSlots : LayoutKind -> List StorageKind -> Bool
validSlots ConstructorCell (RawScalar :: fields) = allTagged fields
validSlots ClosureCell (RawScalar :: CodeAddress :: captures) =
  allTagged captures
validSlots WordArray (RawScalar :: fields) = allTagged fields
validSlots DynamicWordArray [RawScalar, TaggedWord] = True
validSlots AtomicBox [RawScalar, RawScalar] = True
validSlots AtomicByteBlock [RawScalar, RawScalar, PackedBytes] = True
validSlots _ _ = False

export
validateEvent : NativeEvent -> List String
validateEvent (Allocation _ layout _ _ extent slots _ _) =
  if extent == "" then
    ["allocation has no extent"]
  else if validSlots layout slots then
    []
  else
    ["allocation storage disagrees with its native layout"]
validateEvent (Call _ name _ args kinds output callEffect) =
  let (expected, expectedOutput, expectedEffect) = helperContract name
  if expectedEffect == UnknownEffect then
    if callEffect == UnknownEffect || callEffect == MayCollectAndReenter then
      []
    else
      ["unclassified call was declared collection-free"]
  else if kinds == expected
    && output == expectedOutput
    && callEffect == expectedEffect
    && listLen args == listLen kinds then
    []
  else
    ["runtime call disagrees with its native ABI contract"]
validateEvent (Store _ _ _ _ TaggedWord) = []
validateEvent (Store _ _ _ _ _) =
  ["Ref mutation must store a tagged value word"]
validateEvent _ = []

storageName : StorageKind -> String
storageName TaggedWord = "tagged-value-word"
storageName RawScalar = "raw-scalar"
storageName CodeAddress = "code-address"
storageName PackedBytes = "packed-raw-bytes"
storageName StackAddress = "stack-address"
storageName NoValue = "void"
storageName UnknownStorage = "unknown"

layoutName : LayoutKind -> String
layoutName ConstructorCell = "constructor"
layoutName ClosureCell = "closure"
layoutName WordArray = "word-array"
layoutName DynamicWordArray = "word-array-repeated-tagged-elements"
layoutName AtomicBox = "atomic-box"
layoutName AtomicByteBlock = "atomic-byte-block"

callEffectName : CallEffect -> String
callEffectName NoManagedCollection = "no-managed-collection-no-callback"
callEffectName MayCollect = "may-collect-no-callback"
callEffectName MayCollectAndReenter = "may-collect-and-reenter"
callEffectName UnknownEffect = "unknown-may-collect-and-reenter"

node : String -> List String -> String
node tag fields = "(" ++ joinWith " " (tag :: fields) ++ ")"

strings : List String -> String
strings xs = node "operands" (map escStr xs)

slotsText : List StorageKind -> String
slotsText xs = node "storage" (map storageName xs)

eventText : NativeEvent -> String
eventText (Allocation scope kind pointer word extent slots inputs init) = node
  "allocation"
  [
    escStr scope,
    layoutName kind,
    escStr pointer,
    escStr word,
    escStr extent,
    slotsText slots,
    strings inputs,
    escStr init,
  ]
eventText (Call scope name result args kinds output callEffect) = node "call" [
  escStr scope,
  escStr name,
  escStr result,
  strings args,
  slotsText kinds,
  storageName output,
  callEffectName callEffect,
]
eventText (Operand scope word kind) =
  node "operand" [escStr scope, escStr word, storageName kind]
eventText (Store scope owner offset word kind) = node "store" [
  escStr scope,
  escStr owner,
  intToString offset,
  escStr word,
  storageName kind,
]
eventText (Derived scope address base offset) =
  node "derived" [escStr scope, escStr address, escStr base, escStr offset]
eventText (Uncovered scope producer) =
  node "uncovered" [escStr scope, escStr producer]

binderText : BinderRow -> String
binderText row = match row.brId
  BinderId module_ ordinal => node "semantic-binder" [
    escStr module_,
    intToString ordinal,
    escStr row.brName,
    runtimeTypeName row.brType,
    match row.brReturns
      Some t => runtimeTypeName t
      None => "no-return-fact",
  ]

eventGaps : NativeEvent -> List String
eventGaps (Call scope name _ _ _ _ UnknownEffect) =
  ["unknown call contract: \{scope}: \{name}"]
eventGaps (Derived scope _ _ _) =
  ["heap-derived address requires relocation proof: \{scope}"]
eventGaps (Uncovered scope producer) =
  ["uncovered producer: \{scope}: \{producer}"]
eventGaps (Allocation scope _ _ _ _ _ _ "deferred-backpatch") =
  ["deferred initialization requires publication proof: \{scope}"]
eventGaps _ = []

export
renderContract : List BinderRow -> List NativeEvent -> Result String String
renderContract binders events =
  let faults = flatMap validateEvent events
  if listLen faults > 0 then
    Err (joinNl faults)
  else
    let gaps =
      [
          "partial producer inventory: runtime families outside ByteBlock/bit and unhooked call paths are not covered",
          "root liveness, temporary roots and reloads are not produced",
          "C helper roots, uintptr_t root-slot ABI and allocating callback reentry are not established",
          "static/global ownership and barriers are not established",
          "tagged value words identify storage, not scalar types or membership in the managed heap",
        ]
        ++ flatMap eventGaps events
    Ok
      (joinNl
          ([
              node "native-contract" [
                "v1", "boehm", "incomplete", "moving-safe=false"
              ],
              node "foreign-layout-obligation" [
                "mdk_gc_byteblock_atomic_v1", "runtime-owned-extent",
                "atomic-mask-zero", "experimental-only"
              ],
              node "foreign-root-obligation" [
                "mdk_byteblock_copy", "source-argument=1",
                "Word-slot-before-allocation",
                "reload-before-source-derivation",
                "caller-reuse-needs-caller-roots"
              ],
            ]
            ++ map binderText binders
            ++ map eventText events
            ++ map (gap => node "gap" [escStr gap]) gaps)
        ++ "\n")

{- | The host primitives.

   Every name here is an `extern` implemented by the runtime, in scope in
   every program without an import. Most have a friendlier form in a
   library module (`string.toUpper` over `stringToUpper`, `io.readLines`
   over `readFile`); use this page when no library module covers what you
   need.

   An effect on a return type (`<Stdout>`, `<FileRead>`, `<Net>`,
   `<IO>`) names what the primitive touches. A primitive with no effect is
   pure. Mutation of a `Ref` or an array carries no effect. -}

-- Every name here must have a matching implementation in the native
-- interpreter, compiler/eval/eval.mdk.  To add a new primitive: add an
-- extern line here, add its implementation to eval.mdk's primitive dispatch,
-- and (if non-pure) its effect annotation here ensures eff_env is seeded
-- automatically.  See .claude/skills/add-primitive/SKILL.md for the full
-- procedure, including the LLVM/WasmGC backend wiring a primitive that must
-- also work under `medaka build` needs.
--
-- `pure` and `map` are not externs: they're interface methods of Applicative
-- and Mappable declared in stdlib/core.mdk, and dispatched through
-- user-written impl bodies.

-- # Output

-- `print`/`println` are Medaka functions in core.mdk that render via
-- `Display` and call these.

-- | Writes a string to standard output.
extern putStr : String -> <Stdout> Unit

-- | Writes a string and a newline to standard output.
export
extern putStrLn : String -> <Stdout> Unit

-- | Writes a string to standard error.
extern ePutStr : String -> <Stderr> Unit

-- | Writes a string and a newline to standard error.
extern ePutStrLn : String -> <Stderr> Unit

-- | Flushes buffered standard output.
extern flushStdout : Unit -> <Stdout> Unit

-- # Input

-- | Reads one line from standard input, without its newline. Bytes that are
-- not valid UTF-8 read as U+FFFD, one per ill-formed sequence.
extern readLine : Unit -> <Stdin> String

-- | Reads one line from standard input, or `None` at end of input. Bytes
-- that are not valid UTF-8 read as U+FFFD, one per ill-formed sequence.
extern readLineOpt : Unit -> <Stdin> Option String

-- | Reads all of standard input. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 read as
-- U+FFFD, one per ill-formed sequence.
extern readAll : Unit -> <Stdin> String

-- | Reads exactly the given number of bytes from standard input, or `None`
-- at end of input or on a short read. Like every string read from outside the
-- program, each ill-formed UTF-8 sequence becomes U+FFFD, so the result's
-- UTF-8 length can differ from the count.
extern readExactly : Int -> <Stdin> Option String

-- # Mutable references

-- | A new mutable cell holding a value. Read it with `!r` and write it
-- with `r := v`.
export
extern Ref : a -> Ref a

-- # Files

-- | The contents of a file as a string, or `Err` with the host's message.
-- A file that is not valid UTF-8 is an `Err` naming the path; read it with
-- `readFileBytes`.
extern readFile : (path : String) -> <FileRead path> Result String String

-- | The contents of a file as bytes, `0` to `255` each, or `Err` with the
-- host's message.
extern readFileBytes : (path : String) ->
  <FileRead path> Result String (Array Int)

-- | Writes a string to a file, replacing any existing contents.
extern writeFile : (path : String) ->
  String ->
  <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Writes bytes, `0` to `255` each, to a file, replacing any existing
-- contents.
extern writeFileBytes : (path : String) ->
  Array Int ->
  <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Writes a string to a file, replacing any existing contents, and leaves
-- the file at exactly the permission bits the given mode names (`384` is
-- `rw-------`, `420` is `rw-r--r--`).
--
-- The contents never exist at a wider mode: the mode is set on the open
-- file before the first byte is written, so neither the process umask nor a
-- pre-existing file's own mode can widen the result.
extern writeFileMode : (path : String) ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Appends a string to a file, creating it when it does not exist.
extern appendFile : (path : String) ->
  String ->
  <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Whether a path exists.
extern fileExists : (path : String) -> <FileRead path> Bool

-- | A path's permission bits, `0` to `4095` (`384` is `rw-------`), or
-- `Err` with the host's message. Symbolic links are followed.
extern fileMode : (path : String) -> <FileRead path> Result String Int

-- | The absolute path with `.`, `..`, and symbolic links resolved. The
-- input, unchanged, when it cannot be resolved. A resolved path whose bytes
-- are not valid UTF-8 reads with U+FFFD in their place, and so may not name
-- the entry it came from.
extern canonicalizePath : (path : String) -> <FileRead path> String

-- | The names of the entries in a directory. A name whose bytes are not
-- valid UTF-8 reads with U+FFFD in their place, so two such names can read
-- alike and a returned name may not open the entry it came from.
extern listDir : (path : String) -> <FileRead path> Result String (List String)

-- | Creates a directory.
extern makeDir : (path : String) -> <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Deletes a file.
extern removeFile : (path : String) -> <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | Moves or renames a path.

-- | Removes an empty directory.
extern removeDir : (path : String) -> <FileWrite path> Result String Unit

-- | A path's size in bytes, whether it is a directory, whether it is a

extern buildFingerprint : Unit -> String

-- | Runs a program with arguments and waits for it. `Ok` carries the exit
-- code, the captured standard output, and the captured standard error; a
-- non-zero exit code is still `Ok`. `Err` carries the host's message when
-- the program could not be started. The captured output is read as UTF-8:
-- bytes that are not valid UTF-8 read as U+FFFD, so output that is binary
-- data does not come back unchanged.
extern runCommand : (program : String) ->
  List String ->
  <Exec program> Result String (Int, String, String)

-- | Runs `program` once for each argument list, at most the given number of
-- runs at a time, and waits for all of them. A number below 1 runs them one
-- at a time. Element i of the result is what `runCommand` returns for the
-- i-th argument list, so results are in input order whatever order the runs
-- finish in. As with `runCommand`, a program that cannot be executed exits
-- 127 with the host's message on standard error, and `Err` means the run
-- could not be started or its exit status could not be read back; either
-- way the other runs still happen.
--
-- > runCommandBatch "sh" 2 [["-c", "sleep 0.2; echo a"], ["-c", "echo b"]]
-- [Ok (0, "a\n", ""), Ok (0, "b\n", "")]
-- > runCommandBatch "echo" 0 [["x"], ["y"], ["z"]]
-- [Ok (0, "x\n", ""), Ok (0, "y\n", ""), Ok (0, "z\n", "")]
-- > map (r => map ((c, o, e) => (c, o, e /= "")) r) (runCommandBatch "medaka-no-such-program" 2 [[], ["a"], ["b"]])
-- [Ok (127, "", True), Ok (127, "", True), Ok (127, "", True)]
-- > map (r => map ((c, o, _) => (c, stringLength o, stringSlice 1048560 1048576 o)) r) (runCommandBatch "sh" 2 [["-c", "yes 0123456789abcde | head -c 1048576"], ["-c", "yes 0123456789abcde | head -c 1048576"]])
-- [Ok (0, 1048576, "0123456789abcde\n"), Ok (0, 1048576, "0123456789abcde\n")]
extern runCommandBatch : (program : String) ->
  Int ->
  List (List String) ->
  <Exec program> List (Result String (Int, String, String))

-- | Ends the program with an exit code.
extern exit : Int -> Unit

-- | Aborts the program with a message. Panics cannot be caught.
extern panic : String -> a

-- Coded-OOB abort, for a container's own `Index`/`IndexMut` impl to raise on
-- out-of-bounds access.  Reuses the existing E-INDEX-OOB abort machinery
-- every backend already has for the built-in index paths (native @mdk_oob_msg,
-- wasm's E-INDEX-OOB trap), unlike `panic`, which is always coded E-PANIC.
-- Every engine prints the caller's message after the code.

-- | Aborts the program with an index error. For a container's own `Index`
-- instance.
extern indexError : String -> a

-- Prefer this over `indexError` with an interpolated message wherever the
-- container is Int-keyed: building that string costs enough LLVM inline
-- budget to stop `index`/`setIndex` inlining into hot loops, and the guards
-- are on every `a[i]`.  Here the abort formats the index itself (native
-- @mdk_oob_at), so the caller allocates nothing.

-- | Aborts the program with an index error naming the offending index. For
-- a container's own `Index` instance.
extern indexErrorAt : Int -> a

-- Internal: `indexErrorAt` reporting where the read was written.  The first
-- argument is a packed source site (0 for none), which a native build's
-- `Index` impl twins (`arrayIndexAt` and its siblings in core.mdk) carry in
-- from the caller's `xs[i]`; every other engine ignores it.
extern indexErrorAtSite : Int -> Int -> a

-- Internal: `panic` reporting where it was called.  The native lowering writes
-- a located `panic m` as `panicAt <site> m`, the site packed into an Int;
-- every other engine ignores the site.
extern panicAt : Int -> String -> a

-- Args are `(lo, hiIncl)`, the original low bound and the INCLUSIVE upper
-- bound (adjusted end - 1), so the message reads `slice [lo..hiIncl] out of
-- bounds`, byte-identical to the interpreter's `sliceArray` abort.  Reuses
-- the E-SLICE-OOB abort machinery every backend already has.

-- | Aborts the program with a slice error for the inclusive range between
-- its two arguments. For a container's own `Slice` instance.
extern sliceError : Int -> Int -> a

-- Internal `medaka run` plumbing ("run drops stdout on panic" fix). `run`'s
-- tree-walking interpreter buffers a program's stdout in an in-language
-- Ref<String> (eval.mdk's outputRef) and writes it out only after `main`
-- returns normally, so a panicking program's buffered stdout would otherwise be
-- silently discarded (Medaka panics are not catchable; there is no unwind
-- path back to that final write). These two internal-only externs let
-- eval.mdk register the buffer with the native runtime so every abort path
-- (panic / index-OOB / non-exhaustive-match / stack-overflow / a fatal
-- signal) can flush it before dying; see runtime/medaka_rt.c's
-- mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort. Not for general use: `stashRunStdout` takes
-- an O(1) pointer+length snapshot (no allocation, no observable effect by
-- itself) and `enableRunStdoutFlush` is called exactly once, only by the
-- real `medaka run` CLI driver, never by the pure differential-oracle eval
-- probes, which share this same source but never call it, so their captured
-- output is unaffected.
extern stashRunStdout : String -> Unit
extern enableRunStdoutFlush : Unit -> Unit

-- Internal: the terminator of a desugared guard chain.  Raises the same "no
-- clause matched" signal as a failed pattern, so when a function clause's
-- guards all fail, dispatch falls through to the next pattern clause
-- (Haskell semantics) instead of aborting.  Not meant for direct use.
extern __fallthrough__ : Unit -> a

extern assertSnapshot : String -> String -> <IO> Unit

-- # Networking

-- Native-only; unbound under `medaka run`, rejected by --target wasm.  A
-- socket is a `Socket h` or a `ListenSocket a` (declared `extern data` in
-- core.mdk): only the externs below produce one, and each is produced at the
-- authority its opening extern was granted, so an operation on it is charged
-- at that authority.  See NET-DESIGN.md.

-- | The numeric addresses a host name resolves to.
extern netResolve : (host : String) -> <Net host> Result String (List String)

-- | Opens a TCP connection to a host and port.
extern netTcpConnect : (host : String) ->
  Int ->
  <Net host> Result String (Socket host)

-- | Starts listening for TCP connections on an address and port. Port `0`
-- picks a free port.
extern netTcpListen : (host : String) ->
  Int ->
  <Net host> Result String (ListenSocket host)

-- | The port a listener is bound to. Use it after listening on port `0`.
extern netListenPort : ListenSocket a -> <Net a> Result String Int

-- | Waits for the next connection on a listener. The connection is at the
-- listener's authority: it is reached through the address the listener was
-- granted.
extern netTcpAccept : ListenSocket a -> <Net a> Result String (Socket a)

-- | Sends bytes on a connection. The result is the number of bytes
-- written, which may be fewer than given.
extern netSend : Socket h -> Array Int -> <Net h> Result String Int

-- | Sends bytes starting at the given offset into the array. The result is the number
-- of bytes written, which may be fewer than given and is limited to 64 KiB per
-- call so a loop can retain one array while advancing through it.
extern netSendFrom : Socket h -> Array Int -> Int -> <Net h> Result String Int

-- | Receives up to the given number of bytes from a connection. An empty array means the
-- other side has closed.
extern netRecv : Socket h -> Int -> <Net h> Result String (Array Int)

-- | Shuts down one or both directions of a connection: `0` for reading,
-- `1` for writing, `2` for both.
extern netShutdown : Socket h -> Int -> <Net h> Result String Unit

-- | Closes a connection.
extern netClose : Socket h -> <Net h> Result String Unit

-- | Closes a listener.
extern netCloseListener : ListenSocket a -> <Net a> Result String Unit

-- | Sets a connection's send and receive timeout in milliseconds. `0`
-- means no timeout.
extern netSetTimeout : Socket h -> Int -> <Net h> Result String Unit

-- | The descriptor number of a connection, for `ioPoll`. The number grants
-- nothing: every other extern takes the socket itself.
extern socketFd : Socket h -> Int

-- | The descriptor number of a listener, for `ioPoll`.
extern listenSocketFd : ListenSocket a -> Int

-- ## Readiness
--
-- The async runtime's non-blocking half (`stdlib/async.mdk`, `net_async`).
-- Would-block is `Ok None`; `Ok (Some x)` carries what the blocking sibling
-- returns; `Err` is the host's error message.

-- | Installs an opt-in SIGTERM handler for a native PDS, returning a pipe
-- descriptor readable on shutdown. A binary that never calls this retains
-- the operating system's default signal behavior. Call once after bind.
extern pdsSignalStart : Unit -> <Signal> Result String Int

-- | Whether SIGTERM has been observed since `pdsSignalStart`. Stays true;
-- the descriptor remains readable. Only call from ordinary task context.
extern pdsSignalRequested : Unit -> <Signal> Bool

-- | Waits until any of the descriptors is ready, or the timeout in
-- milliseconds passes (`-1` waits forever). The interests are parallel to the
-- descriptors: bit 1 asks for readable, bit 2 for writable. The result is parallel too: bit 1 readable, bit 2 writable,
-- both bits on an error or hangup so a retry surfaces the error. A wait
-- reaches no endpoint: it reads and writes nothing on any descriptor it
-- watches, so it is a timed wait, charged as the clock.
extern ioPoll : Array Int ->
  Array Int ->
  Int ->
  <Clock> Result String (Array Int)

-- | Switches a connection's non-blocking mode on or off.
extern netSetNonblock : Socket h -> Bool -> <Net h> Result String Unit

-- | Switches a listener's non-blocking mode on or off.
extern netSetNonblockListener : ListenSocket a ->
  Bool ->
  <Net a> Result String Unit

-- | `netTcpAccept` that returns `None` instead of blocking.
extern netTryAccept : ListenSocket a ->
  <Net a> Result String (Option (Socket a))

{- | `netTcpConnect` that returns as soon as the handshake is under way. The
   result is a non-blocking socket that is not connected yet: wait for it
   to become writable, then ask `netConnectCheck` whether it arrived. Name
   resolution still blocks. -}
extern netConnectStart : (host : String) ->
  Int ->
  <Net host> Result String (Socket host)

{- | Whether a socket from `netConnectStart` has finished its handshake.
   `None` means not yet, so a woken task asks again rather than trusting the
   wake. `Err` is the handshake's own failure (a refused or unreachable peer)
   and leaves the socket for the caller to close. -}
extern netConnectCheck : Socket h -> <Net h> Result String (Option Unit)

-- | `netRecv` that returns `None` instead of blocking. `Some []` is end of
-- stream.
extern netTryRecv : Socket h ->
  Int ->
  <Net h> Result String (Option (Array Int))

-- | `netTryRecv` delivering the chunk as a packed block, one byte per byte
-- rather than one boxed word per byte. `Some` an empty block is end of
-- stream. The block is allocated for this call alone and reaches the caller
-- with no other reference to it.
extern netTryRecvBytes : Socket h ->
  Int ->
  <Net h> Result String (Option ByteBlock)

-- | `netSend` that returns `None` instead of blocking. `Some n` is the count
-- written, which may be short.
extern netTrySend : Socket h -> Array Int -> <Net h> Result String (Option Int)

-- | `netTrySend` starting at the given offset into the array, sending at most 64 KiB
-- per call, so a loop over a large payload pays only for the bytes it sends.
extern netTrySendFrom : Socket h ->
  Array Int ->
  Int ->
  <Net h> Result String (Option Int)

{- | Sends the bytes of a block in the window between two indices, from the
   first index up to but not including the second, at most 64 KiB per call.
   The result is the number of bytes written, which may be fewer than asked
   for.

   A window outside the block, where the first index is negative, the second
   is less than the first, or the second is past the block's length, is
   `Err`. Unlike `netSendFrom`, which clamps its offset, the window is not
   clamped: a window outside the block is a caller's mistake, and clamping
   would hide it. -}
extern netSendBytesFrom : Socket h ->
  ByteBlock ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  <Net h> Result String Int

{- | `netSendBytesFrom` that returns `None` instead of blocking. `Some n` is
   the count written, which may be short. A window outside the block is `Err`,
   as for `netSendBytesFrom`. -}
extern netTrySendBytesFrom : Socket h ->
  ByteBlock ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  <Net h> Result String (Option Int)

parser.add_argument('--record-build', action='store_true', help='explicitly force-build the oracle and record its actual source/binary binding')

    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

    return {str(p):digest(p) for p in paths}

    if matrix_input_hashes(paths) != expected:
        raise RuntimeError('matrix collector/helper/fixture source drift')

    paths = [*ROOT.joinpath('compiler').rglob('*.mdk'),*ROOT.joinpath('stdlib').rglob('*.mdk'),
             *ROOT.joinpath('compiler').rglob('medaka.toml'),*ROOT.joinpath('stdlib').rglob('medaka.toml'),
             *ROOT.joinpath('runtime').rglob('*.c'),*ROOT.joinpath('runtime').rglob('*.h'),
             *ROOT.joinpath('test').glob('build*.sh'), ROOT/'test/lib_scratch.sh',
             ROOT/'test/emitter_source_set.awk',ROOT/'Makefile']
    return {str(p.relative_to(ROOT)):digest(p) for p in paths if p.is_file()}

    if args.build_manifest.exists(): parser.error('build manifest must not already exist')

    p = subprocess.run(build_command,cwd=ROOT,env={**env,'FORCE':'1','JOBS':'1'},capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=600)
    if p.returncode: raise RuntimeError(p.stderr)
    assert before == source_hashes() and builders == {name:digest(ROOT/name) for name in builders}
    args.build_manifest.write_text(json.dumps({'cwd':str(ROOT),'argv':build_command,'exit':p.returncode,
        'environment':{'FORCE':'1','JOBS':'1'},'stdout':p.stdout,'stderr':p.stderr,
        'sources':before,'builders':builders,'emitter_sha256':digest(args.emitter)},indent=2)+'\n')
    print(args.build_manifest)
    sys.exit(0)

build = json.loads(args.build_manifest.read_text())
def verify_build():
    assert build['sources'] == source_hashes() and build['emitter_sha256'] == digest(args.emitter)
    assert build['builders'] == {name:digest(ROOT/name) for name in ('medaka','medaka_emitter')}
    assert args.emitter.resolve() == (ROOT/'test/bin/llvm_emit_typed_main').resolve()
    assert build['cwd'] == str(ROOT) and build['exit'] == 0
    assert build['argv'] == build_command
    assert build['environment']['FORCE'] == '1' and build['environment']['JOBS'] == '1'
verify_build()

def run(argv, extra=None, success=True):
    current = {**env, **(extra or {})}
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([str(x) for x in argv], cwd=ROOT, env=current,
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        stdout = error.stdout or b''

        records.append({'argv':[str(x) for x in argv],'extra_environment':extra or {},'exit':None,'timeout_seconds':600,
                        'stdout_sha256':hashlib.sha256(stdout if isinstance(stdout,bytes) else stdout.encode()).hexdigest(),
                        'stderr':stderr.decode(errors='replace') if isinstance(stderr,bytes) else stderr})
        with (args.output/'attempts.jsonl').open('a') as journal:
